considered_not_added.reason: Already on the confirmed tab; refuted as stellar rotation/activity by Ribas et al. 2023, A&A 670, A139 (Table 4 'Rotation', Sect. 5, Fig. 8). Reported under incidental_finds for the writer.

considered_not_added.name: HD 238090 ~106 d RV signal
considered_not_added.reason: Authors attribute it to stellar activity: residual peak FAP ~1e-2 at 106.4 d, below their detection threshold, within 3 sigma of the 96.7 +/- 3.7 d rotation period, with a CCF-FWHM counterpart; 'we regard the 106 d signal as caused by stellar activity' (Stock et al. 2020, A&A 643, A112, Sect. 6.4). A GP fits as well as a Keplerian; not called a candidate.

considered_not_added.name: L 168-9 (GJ 4332) RV quadratic drift
considered_not_added.reason: Mignon et al. 2024 (A&A 689, A32, Table B.2) fit a quadratic drift (slope -310773 +/- 127431 m/s/yr, quadratic term 970.85 +/- 398.06 m/s/yr^2, peak-to-peak 15.05 m/s) over a span of only 63 d, about two rotation periods (Prot 29.8 d, Astudillo-Defru et al. 2020). The paper uses it as a long-term correction, says such drifts may be companions and/or activity, and names no candidate. Writer's call whether the trend-only ruling applies; I judge it activity/sampling, not a companion signal.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.finding: Confirmed-tab planet HIP 48714 b (= GJ 373 b, 17.8 d) was attributed to stellar rotation by Ribas et al. 2023 (CARMENES DR1, A&A 670, A139, Table 4 'Exoplanets challenged by CARMENES': GJ 373 b, 17.8 d, Tuo19/Fen20 -> 'Rotation', This work). exoplanet.eu status is now 'Retracted'. NASA still lists it confirmed. Recommend the writer move it to Rejected candidates (or at least flag it).

Confirmed-tab planet GJ 96 b (73.9 d, Hobson et al. 2018) is called spurious by Ribas et al. 2023 (CARMENES DR1, A&A 670, A139): 'the candidates announced around J02222+478 (GJ 96) and J09561+627 (GJ 373) can be quite confidently ruled out as planets'; the 75 d SOPHIE signal is absent in CARMENES, dominant 28.5 d signal is activity. exoplanet.eu status 'Retracted'. Recommend moving it to Rejected candidates.

Beyond the 100 ly cut: Gaia DR3 parallax 32.5879 mas (< 32.616) -> 100.09 ly; the Systems row says 99.87 ly (0.2% off, within 2%, but on the wrong side of the cut). Also, the discovery paper's own title calls GJ 9689 b a 'candidate' at ~half the rotation period (Maldonado et al. 2021, A&A 651, A93), yet it sits on the confirmed tab.

Beyond the 100 ly cut: Gaia DR3 parallax 32.3697 mas -> 100.76 ly (sheet 100.06 ly; 0.7% off). Also a wide co-moving stellar companion, LP 375-24, is reported by Mallorquin et al. 2023 (A&A 680, A76, Sect. 4.2 and App. C), but the Systems row has stars_in_system = 1.

exoplanet.eu lists the ~170 d satellite of the brown dwarf CD-35 2722 b as 'Confirmed' (CD-35 2722 b I). Filed here as a strong candidate because its authors call it 'plausible'; the workbook's Exomoons tab may be the better home. The published Nature numbers (~0.9 MJup Msini, ~170 d) differ from the arXiv v1 numbers (0.743 MJup, 169.45 d) that exoplanet.eu carries.

The confirmed-tab mass for GJ 341 b (4 M_earth) is an UPPER LIMIT, not a measurement: DiTomasso et al. 2025 (ApJ 979, 214) give M < 4.0 M_earth from HARPS RVs; NASA pscomppars pl_bmasselim = 1. The sheet's radius column is blank though NASA gives 0.88 R_earth.

GJ 508.2 b's orbit is unconstrained: Morales et al. 2025 (arXiv:2507.15516, Sect. 5.5) give only lower limits (P >= 5300 d, Msini >= 1.85 MJup, e >= 0.27) and an astrometric true mass of 6.0 +0.7/-1.2 MJup at the minimum period. The confirmed tab's 5300 d / 588 M_earth are those lower limits; the writer may want to mark them as limits.

The Systems row has stars_in_system = 1, but Ross 458 is a close binary: Ross 458 B (GJ 494 B), 88.9 MJup / M7.4 at 4.755 au, P 13.68 yr (Feng et al. 2022, ApJS 262, 21); Gaia RUWE 4.19. Feng 2022 also give the primary 0.511 +/- 0.004 Msun vs 0.6 on the sheet.
